MODULE 5: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-I+I GRAB AND PLAY

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

2 balls per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players work in groups of five. An offensive player will begin in a corner with a defensive player standing in front of them. The player will pass to the initiator who is positioned a single gap away on the wing. As the ball is received, the initiator will put the ball on their inside hip, while placing their outside hand out for the defender to hi-five. The offensive player will sprint to grab the ball while the defender sprints to hi-five the initiator and recover in front of the offensive player in a live 1-on-1. As soon as the first 1-on-1 is played, the next two players start their 1-on-1 in the same format. The initiator should facilitate four games of 1-on-1 before the pairings change in each group and a new initiator is chosen.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Keeping the advantage before the defense recovers to neutral
- Defense recovering from a disadvantage

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Give the defense a hi-five further away to increase the offensive advantage.
- Players have two dribbles to score.
- The facilitator can pivot cueing the offensive player to curl. The defender must chase over - they are not allowed to go under.
- The offensive player is allowed to cut backdoor as opposed to grabbing the ball. In this case, the facilitator must pass the ball. On a cut, the defender does not need to continue sprinting to the defender to hi-five, but must immediately recover.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help players facilitate correctly, placing the ball on the inside hip and their outside hand ready for the hi-five.
- Groups on each basket may stagger to avoid collisions.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Can you push the ball out further to gain enhanced separation?"
- "When is a good time to cut backdoor?"

Load for younger players

MODULE 5: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

VARIABLE SHOOTING

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players work in pairs. They must shoot 6 shots, with the shooter and rebounder staying in the same role. Once 6 shots are taken, both players will change roles. To begin with, players focus on shooting every shot from a different range and location, while passing in a variable manner in different ways and from changing locations and distances.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Use a smaller ball and shoot from a closer distance with younger players.
- Players must shoot with different arcs (low arc, normal arc, high arc).
- Players must shoot from different stances (wide, narrow, one leg, staggered, etc.).
- Players must shoot while performing a different dribble move before each shot.
- Players must shoot out of different movements (e.g. lunges, hops, crawls, hand-stands, etc.).

### SCORING

N/A

### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage players to explore different shooting coordinations
- Remind players to continuously change where they shoot and pass from

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Adaptive shooting

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you make each movement more variable?"

Load for younger players

MODULE 5: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

4-ON-4 CHANGING RIMS GAME

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available full-courts

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per court

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of four players based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The team that gets a point gets to maintain possession and stay on offense: they will need to immediately attack the opposite end of the court. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The changing rims load: when the offense crosses the half-court line, they can change the basket in which they are attacking at any time. The entire team must cross the half-court line to change direction.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure quick changes after one team secures the win and a new team sprints on-court. They do not need to wait for the defense to get ready, but can immediately inbound the ball and commence play.
- Explain the changing rims load.

### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Ball movement
- Emergency transition defense

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- When is a good time to pass in a 2-on-1?
- How can you space the floor effectively?

MODULE 5: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get a point. The losing team rotates off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Maintaining excellent spacing
- Looking to contain defensive match-ups 1-on-1

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you get the most efficient shot?
- How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?
- What can you do to space the floor effectively?

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the lava load), ready to receive the ball.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

MODULE 5: FULL OUTLINE

FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!

TIP-OFF

Basketball School

TIP-OFF

is our opening huddle where coaches welcome the players as a group and set the expectations for the day. The Tip-Off should take no longer than 5 minutes to maximize player attention spans. There are 5 parts that should be covered in every Tip-Off:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!
